follow-up time: Variable, ranging from a week to 3 months
outcome: Need for antenatal interventions (in-utero blood transfusions, thoracentesis)
Need for postnatal interventions (chest drainage, transfusions)
cohort: 30 cases of fetal hydrops diagnosed antenatally at a single institution
finding: Close coordination between the obstetric and neonatal teams was key to good short-term survival of neonates with antenatally diagnosed hydrops, as it allows timely antenatal intervention and anticipation of potential perinatal complications.
mod_finding: Planned caesarean deliveries were performed in the majority of cases (n=11).
